issues.legal_issue: The validating effect of the retrospective provision for property that purported to vest as evacuee property under a repealed law does not depend on a defect in that law or its procedure.
material_facts: The properties had been taken over as evacuee properties under an earlier regional law and remained with the Custodian through the subsequent legal transitions.
The heirs challenged the properties’ treatment as evacuee property, including the procedure by which they had been taken over.
issues.conclusion: The validating provision applied even if the earlier law and the taking over were free of defects; it also cured any defects in the vesting or procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8(2A) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, read with section 8(2), validates property that purported to vest under a repealed law and actions relating to it, whether or not the earlier law or procedure was defective. The non-obstante clause does not limit that effect. The Court relied on The Dominion of India v. Shrinbai A. Irani, Azeemunnisa v. The Deputy Custodian Evacuee Properties, M/s. Haji Ismail Noor Mohammad & Co. v. The Competent Officer, and approved Ahmedbhai Abdulkadar v. The Custodian of Evacuee Property.

predicates.legacy_evacuee_property_case: The proceeding concerns property dealt with as evacuee property under an earlier law that was later repealed.
predicates.property_purported_to_vest_under_repeale: The property purported to vest as evacuee property in a person exercising custodian powers under the earlier law.

issues.definition: When a legacy evacuee-property case concerns property that purported to vest under a repealed law, the property and related custodian actions are deemed valid.

issues.legal_issue: Property taken over under an earlier evacuee-property law remains evacuee property through later legal transitions unless restoration is authorized in the required formal manner.
material_facts: The properties were taken into the Custodian’s possession under the earlier regional law and remained in that possession through the transitions to successor laws.
An order was said to have directed restoration, but it was not produced, and no official-gazette notification authorizing restoration was shown.
The properties were treated as evacuee property under the later laws.
issues.conclusion: The properties continued to be evacuee property and vested in the Custodian under the later law; the alleged restoration order did not establish that their status had ended.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4 and 16(1) of the Junagadh Act, property vested in the Custodian until restoration was authorized by the State Government through a notification published in the Official Gazette. The successor-law provisions, including section 5 of the Saurashtra Ordinance, section 8(2) of the Central Ordinance, and section 8(2) and (2A) of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, continued or deemed the vesting. Haji Ismail Noor Mohammad & Co. supports automatic vesting under the deeming provisions.

rule.if: legacy_evacuee_property_case and property_taken_over_as_evacuee_property and custodian_retained_possession_through_legal_transition and restoration_not_formally_authorized

predicates.legacy_evacuee_property_case: The proceeding concerns property dealt with as evacuee property under successive legal regimes.
predicates.property_taken_over_as_evacuee_property: An authority took possession of the property as evacuee property under an earlier law.
predicates.custodian_retained_possession_through_le: The Custodian continued to possess the property as the governing legal regime changed.
predicates.restoration_not_formally_authorized: No restoration authorization in the required official form was established.

issues.definition: When property taken over as evacuee property remains with the Custodian through a legal transition and restoration was not formally authorized, it continues as evacuee property.

issues.legal_issue: Civil and revenue courts cannot decide evacuee-property status questions or review matters assigned to the Custodian authorities.
material_facts: The heirs brought a civil suit seeking possession and damages, arguing that the property was not evacuee property and challenging actions and orders of the Custodian authorities.
The suit also challenged the refusal to grant a certificate required for seeking restoration, and the relevant administrative orders had not been challenged through constitutional proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The civil court lacked jurisdiction to decide whether the properties were evacuee property, to review the legality or correctness of the Custodian authorities’ actions and orders, or to decide the certificate question; the unchallenged orders had become final.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 28 and 46 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950, make specified Custodian orders final against challenge in ordinary courts and bar civil or revenue courts from deciding whether property is evacuee property, questioning the legality of Custodian action, or deciding matters entrusted to the Custodian authorities. The Court relied on Custodian of Evacuee Property, Punjab v. Jafran Begum. The statutory bars do not displace the constitutional jurisdictions identified by the Court under Articles 226, 32 and 136.

rule.if: civil_suit_or_revenue_proceeding and (evacuee_status_question_raised or custodian_action_legality_challenged or matter_assigned_to_custodian_authority)

predicates.civil_suit_or_revenue_proceeding: A party brings a civil or revenue proceeding concerning property dealt with as evacuee property.
predicates.evacuee_status_question_raised: The proceeding asks the court to decide whether property is or is not evacuee property.
predicates.custodian_action_legality_challenged: The proceeding challenges the legality or correctness of action taken by a Custodian authority.
predicates.matter_assigned_to_custodian_authority: The proceeding asks the court to decide a matter that the governing law assigns to a Custodian authority.

issues.definition: When an ordinary civil or revenue proceeding raises evacuee status, challenges Custodian action, or concerns a matter assigned to a Custodian authority, the ordinary court cannot decide that matter.

issues.legal_issue: Publication of a notification covering property for the displaced-persons compensation scheme extinguishes the former owner’s interest and vests the property in the Central Government.
material_facts: A notification covering the properties was published under the displaced-persons compensation and rehabilitation legislation.
The heirs sought possession of the properties after that notification.
issues.conclusion: On publication of the notification, the former owner’s right, title, or interest in the properties was extinguished, and the properties vested absolutely in the Central Government free from encumbrances.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(2) of the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, provides for the extinguishment and vesting consequences of a published notification. The Court relied on Basant Ram v. Union of India.

predicates.compensation_scheme_property_case: The proceeding concerns property included in the displaced-persons compensation and rehabilitation scheme.
predicates.notification_covering_property_published: A notification covering the property was published under the applicable compensation and rehabilitation legislation.

issues.definition: When a published notification covers property in the compensation scheme, the former owner’s interest is extinguished and the property vests in the government.
